2. Is the suit barred by limitation? 

 8. Mr Ohiullah, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant, submits that the suit having been brought beyond the period of limitation of one year from the date when the goods have been delivered, or discharged from the ship the learned trial Court failed to appreciate and consider in not holding that the suit was hopelessly barred by limitation under Rule 6 of Article 3 of the Schedule of the Carriage of Goods by Sea (Act XXVI of 1925) and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned trial Court is not sustainable in law. Mr Ohiullah the learned Advocate, in support of his contention referred before us Carriage of Goods by Sea Act and the case of Gladstone Wyllie & Company Ltd vs Shahidi Trading Corporation reported in 10 DLR 307 and the case of Karachi Steam Navigation Co Ltd vs Ebrahim Gani reported in PLD 1957 Karachi 315. 

 20. It is not disputed that the suit was filed beyond one year after the date of discharge or the date when the goods should have been delivered, the trial Court also does not dispute the same. But the trial Court erroneously counted the limitation for filing suit for 3( three) years in a case of damage, but under Rule 6 of Article 3 of the Schedule to the Carriage of Goods by Sea Act which has specifically set out the limitation for one year of the ship being discharged from all liabilities in respect of loss or damage and, as such, we find that in the case of loss and damage of the goods the suit is to be brought within the limitation of 1 (one) year as specified under Rule 6 of Article-3 of the. Schedule to the Carriage of Goods by Sea Act. Ii has been set out to the effect that the carrier is discharged from all liability in respect of loss or damage of the goods unless the claim or suit is filed within one year after the delivery of the goods or the date when the goods should have been delivered. 

 21. The above provision is not merely a rule of limitation but a provision of the substantive law, inasmuch as there is an extinguishment of liabilities in certain events. From Exhibit 5 (F) dated 11-12-1976, it appears that the insurance company fixed the period of limitation for claim till 20-4-1977, but they have filed the aforesaid suit on 1-8-1978 beyond the period of limitation i.e. long after the period of delivery of goods and, as such, the suit is hopelessly barred by limitation. The appeal therefore, succeeds. The suit is liable to be dismissed.
